S488.title: POSIX.1-2024 Shell & Utilities §2.9.3 Pipelines (page anchors as 2.9.2 Pipelines, tag_19_09_02 'Exit Status' subsection)

a_pipeline_status_is_last_command.grounds: pipeline exit status = status of last (rightmost) command (pipefail disabled, no leading '!')
a_pipeline_status_is_last_command.quote: The exit status of the last (rightmost) command specified in the pipeline.
a_pipeline_status_is_last_command.note: Table row 'pipefail Enabled=no, Begins with !=no'. POSIX also defines pipefail (enabled case = all-commands derivation), so 'last command' is the default-off rule, not universal.

b_signal_exit_status.grounds: POSIX: command terminated by signal -> exit status greater than 128 (NOT the literal 128+N form)
b_signal_exit_status.quote: Otherwise, if the command terminated due to the receipt of a signal, the shell shall assign it an exit status greater than 128.
b_signal_exit_status.quote_newline_normalised: raw bytes contain one '\n' between 'status' and 'greater'; normalised to a space
b_signal_exit_status.note: Supports '>128' only. Does not state 128+N. The 128+N wording is in the GNU bash source (S489), which was not retrieved.

b_signal_exit_128_plus_N.grounds: command terminated on fatal signal N -> exit status 128+N
b_signal_exit_128_plus_N.quote: When a command terminates on a fatal signal whose number is N, Bash uses the value 128+N as the exit status.
